claim: Forbidden City admission is RMB 60 peak (Apr 1-Oct 31) and RMB 40 off-peak (Nov 1-Mar 31), with Treasure Gallery and Clock Gallery each RMB 10 extra; it is closed Mondays except public holidays and needs 3-4 hours for the main route.
quote: Peak season (Apr 1–Oct 31): ¥60 ... Off-peak (Nov 1–Mar 31): ¥40 ... Treasure Gallery and Clock Gallery each cost ¥10 extra ... Closed Mondays except on public holidays ... Standard visit: 3–4 hours

claim: Forbidden City tickets are released 7 days in advance at 20:00 Beijing time, capped at 40,000 visitors/day with no same-day sales; international visitors must book real-name with passport and bring the original passport to the Meridian Gate entrance.
quote: Tickets are released 7 days in advance at 20:00 ... a daily cap of only 40,000 visitors ... does not sell same-day tickets ... Passport for booking & entry and real-name reservation are required for international visitors ... must bring the original valid passport used to book their tickets to the entrance of the Forbidden City - Meridian Gate

claim: Temple of Heaven combined ticket (Hall of Prayer plus Circular Mound) is RMB 34 high season / 28 low season, or a RMB 15 park-only entry; park opens 06:00-06:30 with monuments 08:00 onward, and a leisure visit takes about 2-3 hours.
quote: Combined ticket ... 34 CNY ... high season (April 1 - October 31) and 28 CNY ... low season ... Basic park entrance ticket is 15 CNY ... Leisure itinerary (approximately 2 to 3 hours)

claim: Since 2024 the Temple of Heaven has moved to a mandatory digital timed-ticket system, especially for foreign visitors who must reserve in advance.
quote: Since 2024, the Temple of Heaven has fully transitioned to a mandatory digital ticketing system, especially for foreign visitors.

claim: Summer Palace entrance ticket is RMB 30 peak / 20 off-season, with a through ticket (entrance plus gardens) RMB 60 peak / 50 off-season; gates open 06:00 (06:30 winter) and a full tour route takes about 3 hours.
quote: Entrance Ticket: 30 RMB (peak season) or 20 RMB (off-season). Through Ticket (includes entrance and gardens): 60 RMB (peak season) or 50 RMB (off-season) ... Gate 6:00-19:00 ... Tour Route A ... (about 3 hours)

claim: Lama Temple (Yonghegong) admission is RMB 25, open 09:00 with last entry 16:00 and gates closing 16:30, operates a mandatory timed-entry pre-booking requiring passport, and a meaningful visit takes 1.5-2 hours.
quote: ¥25 per adult ... 9:00 AM opening time year-round; 4:00 PM last entry; 4:30 PM gates close ... all visitors, including foreigners, must book a specific entry time slot in advance ... passport ... A meaningful visit takes 1.5 to 2 hours

claim: Tiananmen Square is free but requires advance reservation 1-7 days ahead via the WeChat mini-program with passport-based real-name registration, choosing a fixed window (flag-raising, morning, afternoon, or flag-lowering).
quote: the square itself is free to enter ... visitors must reserve their spot 1 to 7 days in advance ... WeChat's mini-program ... your name, passport number, nationality ... flag-raising, morning, afternoon, or flag-lowering ceremony

claim: Tiananmen reservations must be made by 22:00 Beijing time the day before, entry is bound to the chosen time window and a specific gate (Qianmen/South Gate is faster), and foreigners must carry the original passport.
quote: Make your reservation no later than 10:00 PM (Beijing time) the day before ... Your entry is strictly bound to these windows ... Use Qianmen (South Gate) for faster security checks ... bring your original passport (not a copy)

claim: Mutianyu rates low-moderate crowds and is the recommended first-timer section, while Badaling is rated extremely crowded and not recommended; Jinshanling rates very-low crowds for trekkers.
quote: Mutianyu Crowd Level: Low-moderate, Best For first-time visitors, families, seniors. Badaling Crowd Level: Extremely crowded, Not Recommended (Overcrowded). Jinshanling Crowd Level: Very low, Best For trekkers, photographers.

claim: Mutianyu sees visitor numbers 60-70% lower than Badaling and sits 70 km northeast of Beijing in Huairou, a 1.5-2 hour drive, versus Badaling's 20-minute high-speed train.
quote: Mutianyu offers visitor numbers 60-70% lower than overcrowded Badaling. High-speed trains serve Badaling in 20 minutes from Beijing North Station, while Mutianyu requires tourist buses or private transport taking 90-120 minutes.

claim: Mutianyu entrance is 40 yuan, shuttle bus 15 yuan round trip, and cable-car-up + toboggan-down costs 200 yuan; the wall is ~65 km / 1.5-hour drive from central Beijing.
quote: Entrance: Adults 40. Shuttle bus (round trip): 15. Cable car one-way + Toboggan one-way: 200. Located approximately 65 kilometers from the city center, with a 1.5-hour drive.

claim: Mutianyu DIY public route is Bus 916 Express from Dongzhimen hub to Huairou (70-90 min, ~12 yuan with transit card) then local H23/H24 minibus 20 min to the ticket office; last 916 back leaves around 7pm.
quote: take Bus 916 at Dongzhimen Public Transport Hub... the fare is 12 yuan using a Beijing Transportation Card... ride to Huairou Beidajie takes about 70 to 90 minutes... transfer to the local H23 or H24 minibus for the final 20-minute run. The last 916 back from Huairou leaves around 7:00 PM.

claim: The Mutianyu toboggan is 1,580 meters long with a 260-meter drop, with a slow lane for children and a fast lane reaching up to 40 km/h.
quote: The Toboggan is 1,580 meters long with a 260-meter drop and has a slow lane for children (accompanied by adults) and a fast lane reaching up to 40 km/h for adrenaline seekers.

claim: Jinshanling tickets are 65 RMB summer / 55 RMB winter and Gubeikou ~33 RMB; the area is ~2.5 hours / 135 km northeast of Beijing, mixes restored and wild wall, and the 10 km Gubeikou-Jinshanling hike (4-6 hrs) works as a same-day trip.
quote: Jinshanling: 65 RMB (summer); 55 RMB (winter). Gubeikou: 33 RMB. Approximately 2.5 hours northeast from the capital, covering about 135 kilometers... The standard route spans roughly 10 kilometers and requires 4-6 hours... Yes, this works as a same-day excursion.

claim: Guided one-day Jinshanling/Simatai-West hiking tours pick up at Beijing hotels around 7-8am with a 2.5-hour drive each way, ~3 hours hiking, returning 17:00-18:00.
quote: Pick-up at your hotel is at 8am, and hiking starts around 10:30 am, taking about 3 hours to complete. The return to your hotel is at 17:00 - 18:00 depending on traffic. The drive is 2.5 hours to Jinshanling East (Simatai West).

claim: Simatai is ~120 km / 2-hour drive from downtown Beijing, adjoins Gubei Water Town, requires advance reservation, and is the only section open for an official night tour with round-trip cable car around 120-160 yuan.
quote: Simatai Great Wall is located in Miyun District, adjacent to the Gubei Water Town, 120 kilometers away from downtown Beijing, about a two-hour drive. Night tour costs CNY160 for round-trip cable car access... a special price of CNY 120 for the Great Wall.

claim: Nanluoguxiang's main street is crowded and touristy with snack stalls and souvenir shops, but its smaller side alleys like Mao'er and Ju'er Hutong stay quiet and authentic with preserved courtyard homes and local residents.
quote: Visitors often overlook the smaller alleyways, such as Mao'er Hutong and Ju'er Hutong, which offer a quiet escape with preserved courtyard homes, local residents, and a calmer, more authentic vibe.

claim: The Gulou (Drum & Bell Tower) area is one of Beijing's most vibrant artistic neighborhoods, a hub of indie cafes, record shops, design studios and microbreweries; you can wander from touristy Nanluoguxiang into a locals' Beijing of dumpling shops and tea houses.
quote: Gulou is one of Beijing's most vibrant and artistic neighborhoods, serving as a hub of indie cafés, record shops, design studios, microbreweries, and creative spaces.

claim: More authentic, less-crowded hutong alternatives to Nanluoguxiang include Wudaoying, Beiluoguxiang (just north, no tour groups), and Caochang Hutong (clean, quiet, uncommercialized with many locals still living there).
quote: Just north of the ever-popular Nanluoguxiang, this alley offers a softer, slower experience that feels more like everyday Beijing, and you won't find tour groups here.

claim: 798 Art Zone is a thriving cultural hub with over 200 galleries and museums hosting nearly 80 exhibitions monthly; anchor galleries are UCCA Center for Contemporary Art, Hive Center, Beijing Commune and Galleria Continua, with galleries open 10am-6pm and closed Mondays.
quote: Today's 798 is a thriving cultural hub with over 200 galleries, museums and avant-garde installations. Explore diverse contemporary art in nearly 80 monthly exhibitions.

claim: Jingshan Park is a 45m artificial Ming-dynasty hill directly north of the Forbidden City; its Wanchun Pavilion offers the best panoramic Forbidden City view plus sightlines to Beihai's White Pagoda, Drum and Bell Towers, with sunset the prime photo time.
quote: From Wanchun Pavilion, you can overlook the entire Forbidden City, as well as see the White Pagoda in Beihai Park, the Drum Tower, the Bell Tower, the Olympic Tower, and other iconic buildings in Beijing.

claim: Jingshan Park is an official Beijing municipal park; in 2024 it was inscribed as a UNESCO World Cultural Heritage site as part of the Beijing Central Axis.
quote: Jingshan Park - Beijing

claim: Beihai Park's signature sights are the White Dagoba, Nine-Dragon Wall and Circular City; boating is the must-do activity with 11 docks offering over 400 boats of more than 10 types, and early morning or evening are the best low-crowd times.
quote: The Beihai Park features 11 docks offering over 10 types of boats, including antique-style vessels, lotus-themed boats and row-paddled boats, totaling more than 400.

claim: Houhai Bar Street is a strip of waterfront bars and live-music venues in converted courtyard houses along Houhai Lake in Shichahai; atmospheric but touristy, with the better experience found in the smaller hutong lanes set back from the lakefront, and live performers from around 8:30pm.
quote: The best venues are typically slightly set back from the main lakefront path, in the small hutong lanes perpendicular to the water.

claim: No Beijing bar made Asia's 50 Best Bars 2025; the highest-ranked mainland Chinese bar was CMYK from Changsha at No. 16, with only a handful of mainland spots in the Top 100.
quote: Asia's 50 Best Bars 2025: Hong Kong comes up top again

claim: Beijing's strong but internationally under-recognized cocktail bars include Black Hole and Tiki Bungalow (Gulou), shifter (Jinbao Jie), non-binary (Andingmen), Obstzimmer (Jiaodaokou), Confidential speakeasy (Shuangjing), and YAN Whisky Bar (Qianmen).
quote: Black Hole (Gulou) - Upstairs bar known for creative riffs on classic cocktails plus vinyl and DJ events ... Tiki Bungalow (Gulou) - 16-year-old rum and Tiki bar renowned for quality rum cocktails

claim: Notable hutong bars and breweries include Great Leap Brewing (Beijing's first brewery, 2010, Dou Jiao Hutong), Jing-A Brewery (Qianliang Hutong), Modernista (Baochao Hutong), Libertango (Fangjia Hutong) and The Caterpillar DIY cocktail bar near Nanluoguxiang.
quote: Great Leap Brewing (Dou Jiao Hutong) ... Described as Beijing's first brewery, founded in 2010 by an American brewmaster and Chinese wife.

claim: Top Beijing rooftops with Forbidden City views include Yun Summer Lounge (15th floor of The Peninsula), Mo Bar (Mandarin Oriental Wangfujing), YIN on 12 (New World Beijing, views of Forbidden City, Jingshan and hutongs), and Amber Lounge (Pan Pacific).
quote: Perched on the 15th floor of The Peninsula, Yun Summer Lounge offers a refined Beijing rooftop experience with stunning views over the Forbidden City and skyline.

claim: China's 240-hour (10-day) visa-free transit policy covers 55 nationalities and 60 open ports across 24 provinces, requiring an onward ticket to a third country.
quote: starting June 12, 2025, nationals of Indonesia may enter China under the 240-hour visa-free transit policy ... 60 open ports across 24 provinces (autonomous regions and municipalities)

claim: Beijing Capital (PEK) and Daxing (PKX) are both eligible entry ports for the 240-hour transit policy, which permits tourism, business and family visits but requires confirmed onward travel to a third country/region.
quote: Travelers must hold valid international travel documents and interline tickets with confirmed dates and seats to a third country or region.

claim: As of February 2026, 50 countries qualify for China's 30-day unilateral visa-free entry; Sweden was added Nov 10 2025, and Canada and the UK became eligible Feb 17 2026, with the policy set to expire Dec 31 2026.
quote: As of February 2026, 50 countries are eligible ... Sweden: Added November 10, 2025; Canada and United Kingdom: Both became eligible February 17, 2026 ... set to expire on December 31, 2026.

claim: Most EU/Schengen nationalities (France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Netherlands, etc.) can enter China visa-free for 30 days through December 31, 2026 without needing the transit-only restrictions.
quote: China extends 30-day visa-free entry for EU citizens — until December 31, 2026

claim: Foreigners can bind an international Visa or Mastercard to Alipay and WeChat Pay after passport verification, covering over 90% of merchants; Alipay is generally easier to set up for first-time visitors.
quote: Binding a foreign Visa or Mastercard to Alipay and WeChat Pay allows payment at over 90% of merchants ... Alipay is more friendly than Wechat Pay for foreigners.

claim: PEK's Airport Express to Dongzhimen takes ~30 min and costs ¥25; Daxing's Express to Caoqiao takes ~22 min at 160 km/h for ¥25; DiDi from either airport runs roughly ¥180–280 to central Beijing.
quote: The PEK Airport Express to Dongzhimen takes 30 minutes and costs ¥25 ... The Daxing Airport Express to Caoqiao takes 22 minutes, costs ¥25 ... Daxing's Express runs at 160 km/h

claim: PEK (32 km northeast) suits classic central/northeast tourist zones while PKX (46 km south) suits the city's southern/western side; DiDi works identically at both airports.
quote: Pick PEK if you are staying in the classic tourist and business zones of northeast or central-east Beijing. Pick PKX if your priority is a more predictable train-based transfer

claim: Travel eSIMs use roaming connections that bypass the Great Firewall, so Instagram, Gmail, WhatsApp and Google work without a VPN; eSIMs are legal for tourists.
quote: All travel eSIMs currently available for China use roaming connections, so they are not affected by the Great Firewall—while staying in mainland China, you can use Instagram, X (Twitter), Gmail, and other apps and services

claim: Google services, WhatsApp, Facebook, Instagram and X are blocked on local Chinese networks; if relying on a VPN instead of an eSIM, install it before arrival since VPN sites are blocked inside China.
quote: Google (including Search, Maps, Gmail), WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter ... typically inaccessible on local internet connections ... Download and install your VPN before you arrive in China

claim: Spring (Apr–May) and autumn (Sep–Oct) are the best times to visit Beijing with mild 11–25°C weather; summer (Jul–Aug) is hot and humid up to 35–40°C, and winter dips to -4 to 4°C.
quote: The best months to visit Beijing are April, May, September, October ... summer ... daily high may reach 35 - 40 degrees Celsius ... Winter is cold and dry, with temperatures usually between -4°C (25°F) and 4°C (39°F)

claim: Beijing's two domestic 'golden week' holidays — May Day (May 1–5) and National Day (Oct 1–7) — bring peak crowds, so weekend visitors should avoid those dates.
quote: China's two golden weeks for tourism: May Day (May 1–5) and National Day (October 1–7)

claim: Siji Minfu is the most-recommended Beijing Peking duck spot at ~CNY 200/person, Da Dong is the Michelin-starred fine-dining option at ~CNY 450/person, and Quanjude is the 150+ year heritage name at ~CNY 200/person.
quote: Siji Minfu... Approximately CNY 200... the restaurant I most often recommend... Dadong Roast Duck... Approximately CNY 450... Michelin-starred restaurant... Quanjude... Approximately CNY 200... history of over 150 years

claim: At Siji Minfu the duck has crispier skin than Quanjude with warmer service, and you should order the pancakes-and-condiments platter (leeks, cucumber, garlic, pickled radish, hoisin, plus sugar for dipping the skin) since duck is rarely eaten alone.
quote: The duck itself was much nicer, with crispier skin than the one in Quanjude... order the pancakes and condiments platter to go with your duck... granulated sugar for dipping the skin... Duck is rarely eaten on its own.

claim: Da Dong uses hung-oven (open-oven) roasting for crispier, leaner skin while Quanjude uses traditional closed-oven roasting for richer, juicier meat; Da Dong's SuperLean duck runs around CNY 398 and a whole Siji Minfu duck is CNY 259 (half CNY 159).
quote: Hung-oven roasting (Da Dong's method) produces a crispier, leaner skin, while closed-oven roasting (Quanjude's traditional method) yields richer, juicier meat... CNY 259 for a whole duck or CNY 159 for a half... SuperLean 5.0 duck costs ¥398

claim: Online consensus treats Siji Minfu as a higher-quality, less-touristy alternative to heritage names Quanjude and Bianyifang; a half-duck set with pancakes and condiments for two runs about CNY 177, and arriving off-peak (around 3pm) or grabbing a WeChat queue number cuts the wait.
quote: growing sentiment that heritage restaurants like Quanjude and Bianyifang can't match the quality of newer establishments like Siji Minfu... a half duck set with pancakes and condiments for two costs around CNY177... dining during off-peak hours around 3 PM, or using WeChat for queue numbers

claim: Jianbing (savory griddle crepe with egg, scallion, cilantro, crispy wonton and hoisin/chili) is a grab-and-go breakfast from morning street vendors and subway-exit stalls, with neighborhood shops at CNY 10-18 versus upscale chains like Mr. Bing at CNY 25-35.
quote: Jianbing... thin layer of batter... brushed with egg... Green onions, fresh coriander, and crunchy wonton crisps... chili or hoisin sauce... local breakfast shops... costing ¥10-18 per piece, while upscale chains like Mr. Bing offer jianbing at ¥25-35

claim: Zhajiangmian (thick wheat noodles in fermented soybean-paste-and-minced-pork sauce with raw cucumber, radish and bean sprouts) is a Beijing signature found at spots like Fangzhuanchang Hutong and Yao's Zhajiangmian for roughly CNY 20-30, while Wangfujing Snack Street is the touristy 500-snack strip.
quote: Zhajiangmian... thick wheat noodles topped with a rich, savory sauce made from fermented soybean paste and minced meat... sliced cucumber, radish, and bean sprouts... Yao's Zhajiangmian... ¥20-30... Wangfujing Snack Street... over 500 types of snacks

claim: Laoshe Teahouse near Qianmen runs nightly variety shows (folk music, Beijing opera, acrobatics, magic) for CNY 80-580 with a CNY 20 minimum tea charge, while Zhangyiyuan Tianqiao Teahouse offers weekend comic-dialogue (xiangsheng) shows at CNY 30-60 including a cup of tea.
quote: Laoshe Teahouse... Evening shows... folk music, Beijing opera, acrobatics, and magic—CNY 80-580... Minimum tea cost: CNY 20... Zhangyiyuan Tianqiao Teahouse... CNY30/40/50/60 per person, including a cup of tea

claim: The Michelin Guide Beijing 2025 lists 101 restaurants including two three-star venues (Chao Shang Chao and Xin Rong Ji), three two-star (including Green Star vegetarian King's Joy), and 24 one-star establishments.
quote: 24 One MICHELIN Star eateries, 3 Two MICHELIN Star establishments (Jingji, Shanghai Cuisine and Green Star King's Joy), and 2 Three MICHELIN Star restaurants (Chao Shang Chao (Chaoyang) and Xin Rong Ji (Xinyuan South Road))

claim: A standard 3-day Beijing itinerary groups Mutianyu Great Wall with Temple of Heaven on one day, Qianmen/Forbidden City/Tiananmen on another, and National Museum plus Summer Palace on a third.
quote: Day 1: Mutianyu Great Wall + Temple of Heaven; Day 2: Qianmen Street + Forbidden City + Tiananmen Square; Day 3: National Museum of China + Summer Palace

claim: Forbidden City, National Museum and Tiananmen Square require booking at least 7 days in advance; Summer Palace and Temple of Heaven at least 3 days ahead.
quote: The Forbidden City, National Museum of China and Tiananmen Square must be booked at least 7 days in advance, while Summer Palace and Temple of Heaven should be booked at least 3 days before going.

claim: Wangfujing is the top base for first-timers, about a 15-minute walk to the Forbidden City and Tiananmen with 5 subway lines, while Qianmen offers a cheaper, more traditional hutong base also within walking distance.
quote: About a 15-minute walk to the Forbidden City and Tiananmen; 5 subway lines pass through. Qianmen: Walking distance to Tiananmen Square and Forbidden City... Traditional Beijing feel, with hutongs, old shops, and local snacks

claim: The recommended Mutianyu sequence is depart Beijing by 7:30 AM to arrive 9:00-9:30, spend 2-3 hours walking the wall, descend by toboggan or cable car, and be back in the city by mid-afternoon.
quote: 7:30-8:30 AM: Depart Beijing; 9:00-9:30 AM: Arrive at Mutianyu; 9:30 AM-12:30 PM: Wall exploration; 12:30-1:30 PM: Lunch; 1:30-3:00 PM: Return to Beijing. A popular combination is 'chairlift up + toboggan down.'

claim: Mutianyu sits roughly 70 km and 1.5-2 hours' drive from central Beijing; tourist buses depart 8-10 AM and Didi runs around 200 RMB each way.
quote: Mutianyu is located only around 70 km from Beijing... BusDa offers reliable departures at 8:00 a.m., 9:00 a.m., 10:00 a.m... Didi is the most comfortable option, with costs around 200 RMB (~25€) one way

claim: Exit the Forbidden City via the northern Gate of Divine Prowess and walk 5 minutes to Jingshan Park, where a ~10-minute climb gives the classic panorama back over the palace roofs, best in late afternoon light.
quote: From the exit of the Forbidden City, Jingshan Park is just a 5 minute walk... The climb takes about 10 minutes. At the top, you get the classic view of the Forbidden City... Time your visit to the late afternoon

claim: A 2-day Beijing plan covers Tiananmen, Forbidden City, Temple of Heaven, Summer Palace, a Great Wall hike and a hutong rickshaw ride, but guides flag it as rushed and recommend 3+ days for a relaxed pace.
quote: A typical 2-day itinerary includes Tiananmen Square, the Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven, the Summer Palace, a hike on the Badaling Great Wall, and a rickshaw ride through Hutong alleys... a 3 to 6-day tour is recommended

claim: Most visitors spend two to three hours inside the Forbidden City entering at the Meridian Gate (south) and exiting at the Gate of Divine Prowess (north), with up to four hours if exploring side courtyards.
quote: Most people spend two to three hours inside the Forbidden City, and if you explore the side courtyards and take your time, you can easily spend four hours.

claim: Donglaishun (founded 1903) is the landmark Beijing instant-boiled-mutton (copper-pot) hotpot restaurant, with hand-sliced lamb cooked in seconds in a charcoal-fired copper pot and a price of roughly RMB 150-250 per person.
quote: Donglaishun is a renowned Beijing hotpot restaurant famous for its 'instant-boiled mutton' ... established in 1903 ... Approximately 150-250 RMB per person ... hand-sliced lamb, which cooks in seconds
